en.title: Loved The Odyssey? 5 Games That Capture Its Epic Spirit

en.body:
Homer's nearly 3,000-year-old epic, *The Odyssey*, continues to resonate, exploring themes of longing, endurance, hubris, and the very essence of the human condition. Its enduring power lies in its unforgettable characters, thrilling set pieces, and the captivating blend of horror and magic inherent in Greek mythology. If the idea of navigating treacherous seas and confronting inner demons, much like Matt Damon's character, sparks your desire for an epic quest, you're in the right place. We've explored the vast digital landscape to find games that capture that same sense of profound adventure and mythological wonder.

## Embark on Your Own Mythic Journey

The most direct connection to Homer's masterpiece is, of course, **Assassin's Creed: Odyssey**. Ubisoft's ambitious title plunges players into a stunningly realized Ancient Greece, allowing them to sail the Aegean Sea, engage with historical figures like Plato and Socrates, and battle legendary creatures. The game truly lets you craft your own odyssey, complete with divine politics and personal epics. For those seeking a more lighthearted yet equally epic mythological adventure, **Immortals Fenyx Rising** offers a vibrant, open-world experience inspired by Greek myths. While its name might not immediately evoke Homer, its gameplay is a delightful journey through a world filled with gods, monsters, and puzzles, providing a fresh perspective on ancient legends.

Beyond these obvious choices, the spirit of *The Odyssey* can be found in other vast, narrative-driven experiences. **The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt**, with its sprawling world, complex characters, and morally gray choices, mirrors the journey of a hero facing overwhelming odds and personal struggles. Geralt's quest to find his adopted daughter Ciri often involves navigating treacherous political landscapes and confronting monstrous foes, echoing Odysseus's determination to return home. Similarly, **God of War (2018)** and its sequel, **God of War Ragnarök**, offer deeply personal journeys set against a backdrop of Norse mythology that feels as epic and dangerous as ancient Greece. Kratos's quest to protect his son and confront his past is a powerful narrative of endurance and familial bonds, wrapped in stunningly brutal combat and a world rich with lore.

## A World of Choices and Consequences

These games resonate with fans because they don't just replicate the *setting* of ancient epics; they capture the *feeling*. They offer players agency in vast worlds where choices have weight, where heroes are flawed, and where the journey is as important as the destination. The sense of exploration, the confrontation with the unknown, and the personal growth required to overcome immense challenges are all hallmarks of *The Odyssey* that these titles expertly translate into interactive experiences. Players are not just spectators; they are active participants in their own unfolding sagas, much like Odysseus himself.

## What's Next

While specific release dates for future installments in these beloved franchises are always subject to change, the continued success of these mythologically inspired games suggests that developers are eager to explore more epic tales. Keep an eye on announcements from Ubisoft, PlayStation Studios, and CD Projekt Red for potential new adventures that might just scratch that ancient Greek itch.

content_raw: Whether Christopher Nolan’s blockbuster adaptation brought you here or you’re just a lifelong fan of Greek mythology, there’s no denying the timeless pull of The Odyssey. After all, precious few works of literature can claim to be as resonate as the nearly 3,000-year-old text, which explores longing, endurance, hubris, fate, and the human condition with a level of depth that transcends time and culture. It's also just one hell of a story, filled to the brim with memorable characters and set pieces, and all the horror and magic that makes Greek mythology so endlessly fascinating. If watching Matt Damon navigate "the wine-dark sea" and his own guilt-laden mind left you eager to embark on an epic journey of your own, you've come to the right place. From massive open-world adventure games to mind-bending mysteries, here is a list of games you should play if you loved The Odyssey. Assassin's Creed: Odyssey Okay yes, this is an extremely obvious one, but it's obvious for a reason. Ubisoft's fantastic recreation of Ancient Greece allows players to sail the Aegean sea, rub shoulders with the likes of Plato and Socrates, and take down mythological creatures all while crafting their own, well, odyssey. And hey, if you're feeling flirty, you can also smooch a character named Odessa in the game, a self-proclaimed descendent of Odysseus found wandering around Ithaca. With the largest map and deepest RPG systems of any Assassin's Creed game, Odyssey is a sprawling adventure that allows players to truly immerse themselves in divine politics and weave a Homerian epic of their very own. Immortals Fenyx Rising As with AC: Odyssey, Immortals Fenyx Rising is a Ubisoft title and a bit obvious, but it is also criminally slept on. Yes, it's name could be better--and originally was! -- but despite releasing alongside plenty of hard-hitting games back in 2020, Fenyx Rising remains one of the most unapologetically fun titles of that year. If you're looking for an experience with the gameplay sensibilities of The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild but the melodrama, comedy, and humanistic themes associated with Greek mythology, you'd be hard pressed to find a better game to pick up. Titan Quest If you want to feel like an epic hero, carving a path through ancient history and taking down mythical beasts left and right, you can't go wrong with Titan Quest. Set during Greece's Bronze Age, the action RPG tasks you with saving Greece, Egypt, and Asia from total destruction after the ruinous Titans escape from their divine prison. If your favorite part of The Odyssey is the sheer thrill of a grand, world-spanning adventure--or Odysseus's many face-offs against mythological horrors--this classic hack-and-slash is well worth diving into. Ryse: Son of Rome Yes, wrong fallen empire, I know, but if you're looking for a game that captures the brutality of ancient warfare and prioritizes cinematic immersion, Ryse fits the bill.
